result.title: Computation, not weight access: large language models as auditors of clinical prediction networks
result.comment: 13 pages, 2 figures, 6 tables. Code, simulated networks, prompts and replies: https://github.com/Chth1z/llm-clinical-network-audit
result.summary: Frontier large language models (LLMs) have been reported to read, edit and write the weights of small neural networks, raising the prospect of auditing clinical prediction models from their files alone. Public demonstrations, however, mixed reading raw weights with running code. We separated these conditions in internally pre-specified simulation experiments. Tanh networks of 105 to 38,401 weights were trained on simulated cohorts of patients with subarachnoid haemorrhage, each with a planted relationship or none, and one network was trained on labels that under-recorded deaths in a subgroup. GPT-6 Astra and four other GPT models answered single prompts under a default or an explicit system instruction, either with the weights in the prompt and no tools, or with a calculation-only tool that exposed the weights (white box) or only the network's predictions (black box). Without tools, Astra recovered planted relationships in 353-weight networks but became unreliable at 3,457 weights, and under the default instruction it declined 11 of 12 audit and repair tasks as unidentifiable; the explicit instruction removed these refusals. With the tool, it recovered the planted relationship in all 29 runs on networks of up to 38,401 weights, raised no false alarm in 15 runs on null networks, and found the biased subgroup in 6 of 6 runs. Black-box access performed as well as white-box access, and other GPT-6 models read as accurately. A well-designed script matched the comparator models on the audit and the best LLM repair. For auditing these networks, what mattered was computation and elicitation, not access to the weights.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把「读权重」与「运行计算」拆成两种条件，让 GPT 系列模型审计模拟临床预测网络，检验它们在无工具时能否从数值权重中恢复植入关系、发现亚组标签偏差，并与仅暴露预测的黑箱访问及脚本基线对比。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「权重可见性并非关键、计算与提示诱导才决定成败」的结论，可供核查 LVR 中模型是否真正使用内部 latent 内容而非依赖外部旁路计算，以及黑箱/白箱访问差异对证据获取与评价设计的影响。
